perturbations.comparison: Java and Rust are structurally equivalent. The class adapter preserves the top/right/bottom/left expansion of Margin 2 8 14 and the document, class, and arrow colors.

Background projection passes, but Java parses Margin 3 7 11 13 as four independent sides while Rust takes only the first scalar. Java places the first component at x=20.08 and produces 284x199; Rust places it at x=10.0786 and produces 277x196.

Colors, fonts, and thickness reach the consumers, and Java does not apply the component Padding value to this symbol. Java emits a shadow filter and stroke-dasharray:7,4; Rust emits neither. The Rust ComponentLineStyle enum collapses the open-ended Java dash grammar, and component_shadow_frontier changes only the canvas estimate without painting a shadow.

findings: Existing evidence improved from review-1's 0/10 boundary to 9/10 strict and 10/10 scoped style semantics. The remaining review1 strict miss is correctly separable from theme/style cascade.

Fresh evidence rejects 99fe75cf: only 1 of 14 heldouts is structurally equivalent. Eleven fail direct style semantics, one fails style-derived component envelope geometry after correct winner selection, and one has exact state style semantics but fails an unrelated direction-layout mechanism.

Java temporal ownership is consumer-specific, not uniformly entity-specific. EntityImageDescription uses Entity#getCurrentStyleBuilder for component and use-case symbol styles; EntityImageState2 uses SkinParam#getCurrentStyleBuilder; EntityImageClass uses the entity builder for body paint while EntityImageClassHeader uses SkinParam's current builder for class-name fonts; GraphvizImageBuilder and SvekEdge use Link#getStyleBuilder for arrows and labels.

Rust's temporal resolver API is sound enough for the previously covered class body and link cases, but its adapters do not preserve Java's ownership graph. Component, state, and use-case call resolve on one final signature, while class applies the entity snapshot to header fonts that Java resolves against the current builder.

Component integration drops per-entity stereotypes, per-link snapshots, arbitrary LineStyle pairs, painted shadows, and clockwise document margins. Taking the first Margin scalar is a direct contradiction of ClockwiseTopRightBottomLeft#read.

Flat state rendering drops stereotype-qualified selectors, header FontColor/FontStyle, document background/margin, and arrow FontColor. Its use of the final state style is correct for EntityImageState2, which the temporal state heldout confirms.
Use-case integration drops per-entity snapshots, stereotype-qualified selectors, arrow LineThickness, and arrow LineStyle. Arrow font family, size, and color do project correctly.
Theme, style, and skinparam winner ordering survives the mixed-order control, but the resulting component canvas envelope remains wrong even when every child element is exact.
The mechanical anti-overfit search is clean, but the provenance gate and generative-model gate both fail. The boundary is not fixture-shaped; it is incomplete and over-generalized.
